\section{Statement, inputs, and parameters}

The retained selected saving is
\[
 \kappa_{\rm old}=0.001672660197076918.
\]
The retained independently replayed supplier lower bounds are
\[
 a_*=0.001733427039589844234749,\qquad
 b_*=0.001675462676808103522925.
\]
Here $a_*$ is the bit saving and $b_*$ is the complex saving. They are supplied inputs, not recomputed finite constructions in this note. Put
\[
 q=b_*-10^{-10},\qquad a_{\rm eff}=(b_*+q)/2,
 \qquad r_0=10^{-6},\quad \zeta=10^{-8},\quad s_0=10^{-5},
 \qquad c_0=3/32.
\]
The effective bit saving is deliberately weakened so that
$q<a_{\rm eff}<b_*<a_*$, matching the convenient ordering in the retained compact recurrence. Define
\begin{align}
 \epsilon&=\frac{1+q+q(c_0-s_0-r_0-\zeta)}{(1+q)^2},\\
 \xi&=\epsilon(1+q)-c_0+s_0,\\
 \beta&=1-\xi-r_0-\zeta.
\end{align}
All displayed finite decimals denote exact rationals. The asserted saving is the exact rational
\[
 \boxed{\kappa=0.001672922349588871
       =\frac{1672922349588871}{10^{18}}.}
\]
The parameters are approximately
\[
 \epsilon=0.998483871108555754,\quad
 \xi=0.906416793468144625,\quad
 \beta=0.093582196531855375.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Conditional capped-fusion transfer]\label{thm:main}
Assume the retained finite bit and complex suppliers, their exact common-frame and mutable-source realization, whole-call row hosting, the semantic precision guard with dimension exponent $C_1=1$, and the retained all-size fixed-tape/prime-packing interfaces. Assume the paid equal-chunk interchange primitive used by the retained support router. Then the deferred-reservation, circuit, Gaussian, and layout constructions detailed below give integer multiplication in
\[
 O\bigl(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\bigr).
\]
The conclusion retains these conditional inputs. It does not assert a new finite supplier, an unconditional arithmetic circuit realization, or a practical finite cutoff.
\end{theorem}

Write $p=\Theta(\log n)$ and let $V=\Theta(n)$ be the live bit volume, with $\Theta(p)$-bit coefficient records. There are $D=d-1=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ resampled axes. Their true source sizes $s_i$ and dyadic target sizes $t_i$ obey the retained capacity bound $T/S<2$, and
\[
 \log s_i=\Theta(p/d),\qquad
 \rho_i=t_i/s_i=1+\theta_i,\qquad
 (4d)^{-1}\leq\theta_i\leq(2d-1)^{-1}.
\]
Each axis eventually exceeds every fixed polynomial in $p$. Choose
\[
 \alpha=\left\lceil\sqrt{\frac4\pi\log(16p)}\right\rceil,
 \quad u=\alpha^2=\Theta(\log p),\quad a=\pi\alpha^2,
 \quad g=\lfloor p^\beta\rfloor,
 \quad B=2^{\lfloor\xi\log_2p\rfloor},
 \quad L=2^{\lceil8\log_2p\rceil}.
\]
The spare power $r_0$ is not the growth rate of $u$: it only provides the eventual bound $u\leq p^{r_0}$. Let $W=O(\sqrt p\,\plog p)$ dominate both physical Gaussian bandwidths, and let $A=C_Ap^3$ be a sufficiently large fixed-constant locality radius. The dense tensor path uses the dyadic $L$-point cores, not a simultaneous padding of $(L+2A)^g$.

Global one-axis coefficient preprocessing is polynomial in $s_i,t_i,p$ and hence $n^{o(1)}$. Local pages regenerated for each coarse block have polynomial cost in $p$ and are charged to that block's superpolynomial $L^g$ payload. These are two different charges.

\section{Dimension-preserving local linear circuits}

The algebraic input is a shallow circuit for a dyadic Toeplitz block on its existing wires. For a Toeplitz matrix within a fixed distance below one of the identity in both row and column norm, the circuit has depth $O(\log^4 B)$, $B\plog B$ invertible two-wire gates, and polynomial prefix and inverse-prefix norms. It needs no clean data coordinate. The broad Gaussian case uses the extension to a symmetric positive definite Toeplitz matrix whose condition number is polynomial in $p$; then prefix logarithmic norms are $O(\log^2p)$, still sufficient here.

For completeness, the construction has the following components. A dirty shear $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+Tx)$ for Toeplitz $T$ splits $T$ into one circulant and one negacyclic circulant. Unitary FFTs, diagonal multipliers, and the inverse FFT implement each shear on the two existing vectors. There is no inverse of a possibly singular Fourier multiplier. A triangular Toeplitz multiplication is split by even and odd coefficients. If $f(z)=e(z^2)+zo(z^2)$, its block factorization has two Toeplitz shears and the two child multiplications by $e$ and $e-zo^2/e$, running in parallel. This gives $O(\log^2 B)$ depth rather than a sequential linear-depth recurrence.

For a full Toeplitz matrix, use $\Delta(M)=ZM-MZ$. Under balanced block elimination, the displacement rank of either child increases by at most one. A shear matrix therefore has displacement rank $O(\log B)$. Its Stein displacement has a bounded-generator decomposition
\[
 T=\sum_j L(g_j)U(h_j).
\]
For one term choose $\gamma\geq2\norm{h_j}_1$ and $P=I+U(h_j)/\gamma$. The sequence
\[
 x\leftarrow Px,\quad
 y\leftarrow y+\gamma L(g_j)x,\quad
 x\leftarrow P^{-1}x,\quad
 y\leftarrow y-\gamma L(g_j)x
\]
adds $L(g_j)U(h_j)x$ to $y$ and restores $x$. The normalized $P$ is a well-conditioned triangular Toeplitz matrix. Combining this compiler with the parallel block recursion gives $O(\log^4B)$ layers. For $mI\preceq G\preceq MI$, all principal Schur descendants retain these spectral bounds. Thus the same construction has log-prefix norm $O(\log B\log(2+M+1/m)+\plog B)$; polynomial bounds on both $M$ and $1/m$ give $O(\log^2p)$.

All coefficients can be generated to the required accuracy in polynomial time in the local size and precision. Exact rational Schur matrices and bounded-generator orthogonalization may use longer offline numbers. Only the rounded bounded data-gate coefficients appear online. See \file{SHALLOW-TOEPLITZ.md}, including its SPD extension, for the full identities, norm induction, and finite controls.

\section{Uniform tensor compilation and the actual supplier call}

Let $N=L=2^m$. A layer of disjoint gates on $N$ wires can be routed to adjacent pairs by a Bene\v{s} network of $2m-1$ switch stages; the reverse route restores its wire order. The stage bit sequence is $0,1,\ldots,m-1,m-2,\ldots,0$. Cycle coloring of the degree-two input/output pair graph gives the switch controls constructively for every permutation.

Put $H=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. Every switch $I$ or Swap has a common two-$H$ diagonal word. Every shear, diagonal, Swap, and FFT butterfly can be written in one common six-$H$ word with bounded invertible diagonal factors. A useful exact seed is
\[
 \diag(-1/8,-1/6)H\diag(2,1)H\diag(-3,1)H
 =\begin{bmatrix}1&5/4\\0&1\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For a shear parameter $t$, use $U(t)=U(t+c)U(-c)$ with $c>2|t|+1$. Both nonzero parameters have controlled inverses, so zero shears cause no singular diagonal. Two- and three-$H$ identity words pad all permitted gate types to the same six-$H$ shape. Thus one original matching layer uses at most $(8m+2)$ simultaneous $H$ stages.

For $g$ different axis circuits, Kronecker multiplication tensors the corresponding $H$ stages and multiplies the diagonal factors. There is no expansion into $2^g$ branches and no data padding. Coarse labels may select different switch and coefficient tables, while the stage schedule stays common. A tensor diagonal has coefficient $\prod_i d_i(x_i)$. In lexicographic order, cached prefix products are recomputed only on odometer carries; the total number of extra products is bounded by $L^g\sum_{k\geq1}k/L^k=O(L^g)$. Scanning the one-axis tables on a fixed number of tapes has the same amortized bound. Consequently each diagonal costs $O(V\plog p)$ rather than $O(Vg)$.

Crucially, an $H$ stage is invoked \emph{globally across all complete coarse-label ranges}. A fixed coarse-label microbox does not contain complete high-coordinate bits to borrow. Each chosen local bit is placed in a complete $K$-bit neighborhood of its original axis, with
\[
 G=4\lceil\log_2p\rceil+6,\qquad K=128G.
\]
An individual neighborhood fits because $K+O(\log p)=o(\log s_i)$. The $gK$ selected positions can be exposed by a permutation supported on at most $2gK$ positions; the complement need not be stably compacted. Coarse labels are restored before the next diagonal is evaluated.

The retained compact supplier's residual basis acts on its selected bits, not on the entire ambient address. Its control shuttles have width $O(hG)$ at a node with $h$ active bits. Reserve whole neighborhoods for the two front fields, one back field, and the full product row stock required by nested bit and complex calls. The completed active call is the desired kernel on active bits and identity on arbitrary dirty reserved coordinates. Thus these reserved selected bits can be deferred, rather than processed individually first. Their count is at most $h/16$ above a polylogarithmic tail. Padding adds whole rows only for the current phase and is deleted before the next one.

The original sufficient wording $K/\log p\to\infty$ is replaced by the finite inequality actually used in its proof, $K\geq G+4\lceil\log_2p\rceil+10$. The present $K$ satisfies it. The support router implements all needed placements with support $O(h\plog p)$, and its short-record construction borrows only $\lceil\log_2p\rceil^2$ suffix bits. It does not move an entire long axis.

Using supplier stopping exponent $10^{-9}$ gives a strict leaf saving above $a_{\rm eff}$ and $q$. The retained stopped recurrence and the geometric sum of deferred widths yield
\[
 O\bigl(Vg^{1-q}\plog p\bigr)
\]
for a complete global selected-bit call, including all exposure/restoration. The retained supplier implements $H_0=H/2$; multiplying by $2^g$ costs one shift scan and $O(g)$ guard bits. The full circuit therefore costs the same bound up to polylogarithms. The derivations and restrictions are in \file{TENSOR-COMPILER.md}, \file{SUPPLIER-SUPPORT-AUDIT.md}, and \file{SUPPORT-ROUTER.md}.

\section{The two actual Gaussian operators}

\subsection{Narrow compression and target-grid completion}
For one axis put $q_j=\lfloor\rho j+1/2\rfloor$ and $\beta_j=\rho j-q_j$. The retained narrow normalized Gaussian is $N=CTD$, where $C$ selects the $q_j$ target rows. Its off-diagonal row sum satisfies
\[
 \norm{N-I}_\infty\leq e^{-2a\theta}+5e^{-2a}.
\]
The two nearest directions must be bounded together; charging each by $e^{-2a\theta}$ would not give this result. With the chosen $a\geq4\log(16p)$ and $\theta\geq1/(4p)$, the row gap is at least $1/(8p)$ eventually. The globally fixed, truncated, structure-preserving rounded matrix $H$ can be chosen with $\norm{H-N}<1/(16p)$, diagonal exactly one, gap at least $1/(16p)$, row norm below two, and $\norm{H^{-1}}_\infty\leq16p$. Every local inverse uses a principal restriction of this same $H$.

Let $E$ inject source coordinate $j$ at target coordinate $q_j$. On the full dyadic target grid define
\[
 H_{\rm aug}=EHC+(I-EC).
\]
It is permutation-similar to $H\oplus I$, so it inherits row dominance and inverse bounds. Its physical target bandwidth is at most $2w+2$, since $q$ increments by one or two. Its inverse on selected rows is $EH^{-1}C$. A diagonal normalization on selected rows, zero on holes, followed by the increasing $q$-image extraction gives exactly the retained compression approximation.

\subsection{Broad expansion}
The broad forward matrix is distinct:
\[
 S_{kj}=\alpha^{-1}e^{-b_0(j-\lambda k)^2},\qquad
 b_0=\pi/\alpha^2,\quad\lambda=1/\rho.
\]
Embed source values at the $q_j$ coordinates, zero elsewhere. Give every hole input column an identity column. The resulting square matrix $M$ agrees with $S$ on the intended zero-hole input. In selected/hole order,
\[
 M=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha^{-1}N_bD_b^{-1}&0\\ R&I\end{bmatrix},
 \quad b=\pi/(\alpha^2\rho^2),\quad
 D_b=\diag(e^{b\beta_j^2}).
\]
The Gaussian row sum of $R$ is bounded. In particular $\norm{M}<3$ eventually; use $M/4$ as the completed forward map, making it contractive also on numerical errors in hole coordinates. Relative to the former $S/2$ normalization this contributes an extra $2^{-D}$ over $D$ axes. A single exact $2^D$ shift compensates it, increasing the retained scalar exponent $\Gamma$ by $D=o(p)$.

On a phase cell $q_j=j+c$, a selected target block has entries
\[
 K_{ki}=\alpha^{-1}e^{-b_0(i-c-\lambda k)^2}.
\]
Its inverse is polynomially bounded even though an uncentered diagonal split can have a large range. The finite Gaussian LDU proof only uses gaps at least one and $|\beta|\leq1/2$. For
\[
 c_b=\prod_{m\geq1}(1-e^{-2b\rho m})
\]
it gives
\[
 \norm{K^{-1}}_\infty
 \leq\frac{\alpha e^{3b/4}c_b^{-4}}
 {(1-e^{-b\rho\theta})^2}.
\]
Indeed $q'_k=k+\rho c$ has unit gaps and $\beta'_{q_j}=\beta_j$. Also
\[
 \log c_b^{-1}
 =\sum_{h\geq1}\frac1{h(e^{2b\rho h}-1)}
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{12b\rho},
 \qquad c_b^{-4}\leq e^{\pi\alpha^2\rho/3}.
\]
Since $\alpha^2=O(\log p)$ and $\theta^{-1}=\poly(p)$, the bound is polynomial in $p$, uniformly over all contiguous cell subblocks.

For a block anchor $m$, set $x=i-m$, $y=k-m$, and $\delta=(1-\lambda)m-c$, with $|\delta|\leq1/2$. The exact Toeplitz split is
\begin{align*}
 K_{ki}&=D_{\rm row}(y)G(y,x)D_{\rm col}(x),\\
 G(y,x)&=e^{-b_0\lambda(x-y)^2},\\
 D_{\rm col}(x)&=e^{-b_0((1-\lambda)x^2+2\delta x)},\\
 D_{\rm row}(y)&=\alpha^{-1}e^{b_0\lambda(1-\lambda)y^2+
                  2b_0\delta\lambda y-b_0\delta^2}.
\end{align*}
The Gaussian Poisson formula bounds the symbol of $G$, with $\gamma=b_0\lambda$, between
\[
 \sqrt{\pi/\gamma}\,e^{-\pi^2/(4\gamma)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad1+\sqrt{\pi/\gamma}.
\]
Thus every finite principal $G$ is SPD with polynomial condition number. Truncating at width $W$ and rounding symmetrically to sufficiently many $Cp$ bits preserve these bounds. The SPD shallow circuit applies. See \file{LOG-A-PHASE-SCHUR-AUDIT.md}, \file{BILATERAL-LDU.md}, and \file{FORWARD-SMALL-A-AUDIT.md} for the analytic details and exact local-identity controls.

\section{Capping and recentering the phase interiors}

All target holes and original physical period cuts are boundary coordinates. Selected target coordinates are consecutive inside an original phase cell, so no interior circuit is applied to a masked Toeplitz matrix. Use the maximum physical bandwidth $W$ for both directions.

In each original $O(d)$-length cell, retain $W$ endpoints and repeatedly choose the largest dyadic interior of size at most $B$ that fits with a following $W$ separator. Once no full $B$ block remains, the dyadic-tail procedure halves the remaining length at every step until its size is $O(W)$, which is all boundary. There are $O(d/B+\log B)$ interiors and
\[
 O\bigl(W(d/B+\log B)\bigr)
\]
boundary coordinates per cell. Since $B=o(d)$, the boundary density is $O((W/B)\plog p)$. Each eliminated interior touches only its two neighboring $O(W)$ boundary groups. Schur fill therefore has half-bandwidth $O(W)$, regardless of the number of capped blocks.

For the narrow exact cell weights
\[
 \omega_j=e^{-a(1/4-\beta_j^2)/\theta},
\]
one step changes their logarithm by $2a\beta_j+a\theta=O(a)$. On a capped block use the exact rounded-weight ratio $\widehat\omega_j/\widehat\omega_m$ around one anchor. The common scalar cancels from the similarity, and its logarithmic range is $O(aB)$. The retained global rounding changes this by $O(1)$, because its $Cp$ precision dominates the original $O(ad)=o(p)$ range. This is symbolic recentering of the same matrix, not a new local rerounding. For the broad split, $|x|,|y|\leq B$ and $B\leq d$ give diagonal ranges
\[
 O\bigl((B+B^2/d)/\alpha^2\bigr)=O(B/\alpha^2)\subset O(aB).
\]
The number of blocks does not multiply circuit depth: they run as a direct sum on the $L$ existing coordinates.

\section{Five factors, sparse windows, and batched boundaries}

For either square operator write $Q=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}A&B_1\\C_1&D_1\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ in interior/boundary order, and $F=D_1-C_1A^{-1}B_1$. Exact multiplication gives
\begin{align}
 Q^{-1}&=\diag(A^{-1},I)E_{-B_1}\diag(A,F^{-1})
                   E_{-C_1}\diag(A^{-1},I),\\
 Q&=\diag(A,I)E_{C_1}\diag(A^{-1},F)E_{B_1}\diag(A,I).
\end{align}
The off-diagonal factors use the original banded $B_1,C_1$. The forward formula uses $F$ only as a matrix application; it does not require a forward Schur inverse or a forward LU-prefix assertion. For the narrow inverse, row diagonal dominance survives elimination. Its Schur row gap stays at least $1/\poly(p)$ and its row norm is bounded, so the retained no-pivot boundary solver applies.

Batch independent right-hand sides in a dyadic width between $W$ and $2W$. A banded triangular solve becomes block updates
\[
 X_j=L_{jj}^{-1}(Y_j-L_{j,j-1}X_{j-1}).
\]
Precomputed diagonal inverses and two square block products implement each update. The seven-product recursion gives exponent $\omega=\log_2 7<45/16$, the latter inequality checked exactly by $7^{16}<2^{45}$. The same batching handles boundary/interior coupling products. Intermediate Strassen additions grow only polynomially in $W$. Round after a completed block update and bound its residual. Each local window has polynomial length $L$, the no-pivot factors and exact partial right-hand sides have polynomial bounds, and the completed system inverse has polynomial norm. Thus the uniform local residual is $\poly(p)2^{-P}$; there is no factor equal to the global number of windows. The total boundary cost is
\[
 O\bigl(V(d/B)W^{\omega-1}\plog p\bigr).
\]

For a group let $J_i$ be its boundary set, and let $E_i$ also include every interior coordinate incident to $B_1$ or $C_1$. Then $|E_i|/L=O((W/B)\plog p)$ and each sparse factor fixes $E_i^c$. The union
\[
 U=\{x\in[L]^g:\exists i,\ x_i\in E_i\}
\]
has fraction $O(gW/B\plog p)$. It is closed under the sparse factors, including a possibly dense inverse on $J_i$. It is \emph{not} closed under a dense $A$ stage. Use two sparse windows, with scatter/regather around the intervening dense stage.

For one sparse axis, $U_i=E_i\times[L]^{g-1}$ is a complete rectangle wholly present in $U$. Scan $U$, extract $U_i$, number $E_i$ in increasing order by a stream counter, transpose only this polynomial-size field, perform its boundary operation, and merge back. Only this one field is temporarily padded, and the padding is deleted before the next axis. Each sparse window costs $O(Vg^2W/B\plog p)$ per group. Across $d/g$ groups this is
\[
 O\bigl(V(dg/B)W\plog p\bigr).
\]
Every group also has a fixed number of full scans costing $O(V)$. Membership calculations use $O(g(\log s)^2\plog p)=o(p)$ bit operations per $p$-bit record. Detailed fixed-tape extraction and batching are in \file{PHASE-LAYOUT-AUDIT.md}.

\section{Core faces, ordered embedding, and precision}

The increasing map $j\mapsto q_j$ permits one product scan for a whole group. Enumerate the dyadic target rectangle. For target $k$, put
\[
 j=\max\{0,\lceil s(2k-1)/(2t)\rceil\}.
\]
It lies in the image exactly when $j<s$ and $2tj<s(2k+1)$. If every coordinate is valid, consume the next source record; otherwise output zero. Lexicographic order is preserved. The inverse scan extracts image records. Intermediate volumes are controlled by $T/S<2$. No per-axis full payload scan is needed.

Schedule all forward q-image group embeddings while the tensor is still in its native axis-major order, before the one global low-bit microbox gather. Keep the complete dyadic target ranges throughout every Gaussian group and every global H call. For compression, perform all group extractions only after the inverse global gather restores native target-axis order. Thus a q-image scan never requires gathering g entire long-axis fields inside the microbox layout, and a supplier call never loses complete coarse-coordinate ranges. The embedding/extraction family costs $O(Vd/g\plog p)$, already included in the group-scan row.

On dense $L$-cores, use principal restrictions of the same rounded augmented matrices. For the narrow inverse, if a row is more than $JW$ from a principal-window edge, the first $J$ powers of $H_{\rm aug}-I$ agree with the global powers on that row. With row gap $1/\poly(p)$ and $J=Cp^2$, the Neumann tails are $2^{-\Omega(p)}$. Choose the fixed constant in $A=C_Ap^3$ large enough for target/source spacing and the row gap. Broad expansion has the simpler truncated-band locality.

Discard dense outputs within $O(A)$ of any core face. Partition these by their first exceptional axis and side. The source-driven rectangular halo construction copies total volume $O(VgA/L)$. It only uses interval geometry, so its copying proof also applies to these position-dependent Gaussian matrices. On the sparse rectangles, apply the retained one-axis local inverse/forward algorithm successively, with the actual coefficients and physical period cuts. Unprocessed axes keep their input halos until used; an erroneous dense edge output is never recycled as a global halo. Padding is only for the currently processed field. A generous per-record upper bound $p^2\plog p$ for each scalar pass gives total correction cost
\[
 O\bigl(V(d/g)(gA/L)g p^2\plog p\bigr)
 =O\bigl(Vp^{\epsilon+\beta-3}\plog p\bigr).
\]
Sparse radix keys have $O(g\log s)$ bits and are paid; they remain far below the main cost. See \file{HALO-THEOREM.md} and \file{PHASE-LAYOUT-AUDIT.md}.

The grouped raw diagonal and local circuit range is
\[
 O(gaB+g\plog p)=o(p),
\]
because $\beta+\xi+r_0=1-\zeta$. A sufficient precision expression is
\[
 P=p+O\bigl(ad+gaB+g\plog p\bigr)=O(p).
\]
The $ad=o(p)$ term is paid once for the inherited absolute coefficient rounding; the current group contributes $gaB$, not $gad$. At the retained sufficiently large constant precision, coefficient and arithmetic accuracy dominate the group prefix/suffix amplification and the polynomial number of compiled stages. Each completed normalized group is contractive; accumulating its errors gives the retained loose $dp^2 2^{-p}$ interface. The extra forward normalization is compensated by an exact $2^D$ shift. The total scalar exponent remains $O(du)=o(p)$ since $\epsilon+r_0<1$.

Local pages can be generated from $O(p/d)$-bit rational origins and $L=\poly(p)$ local indices in polynomial time. Evaluate centered phase expressions and anchored ratios. Raw global squares or unbounded global Gaussian exponentials are not data values. Regeneration per group/coarse block is amortized by $L^g$, avoiding random access to a scrambled global catalogue.

\section{The complete outer ledger}

Deferred reservations also apply to the main synthetic transform. Together with the support-limited global layout replacement they give
$O(V[p^{1-a_{\rm eff}}+p d^{-q}]\plog p)$.
Global chirps and scalar normalizations are separable products and use the same amortized prefix-product scan. Packed polynomial products retain their $\epsilon$ saving. None of these operations retains the former $Vd$ full-scan row.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
Component & Exponent after division by $V$\\
\midrule
Main transform & $1-\epsilon q$\\
Global coordinate routing & $1-a_{\rm eff}$\\
Fused Gaussian groups & $\epsilon-q\beta$\\
Grouped bit routing & $\epsilon-a_{\rm eff}\beta$\\
Group scans & $\epsilon-\beta$\\
Batched boundary algebra & $\epsilon-\xi+29/32$\\
Sparse union movement & $\epsilon+\beta+1/2-\xi$\\
Optional full-key union surcharge & $2\beta+3/2-\xi$\\
Packed polynomial products & $1-\epsilon$\\
Core-face corrections & $\epsilon+\beta-3$\\
\bottomrule

\end{center}
The main and Gaussian savings are equal:
\[
 \epsilon q=1-\epsilon+q\beta
 =0.001672922359588871132465386319946808\ldots .
\]
The boundary saving is larger by exactly $10^{-5}$. Every other row has a strictly larger saving. The chosen rational $\kappa$ is more than $10^{-11}$ below the minimum saving, so fixed logarithmic factors and short-arithmetic overhead can be absorbed. The net gain is
\[
 \kappa-\kappa_{\rm old}=2.62152511953\times10^{-7}.
\]

The independently executable \file{check_capped_outer.py} verifies 44 rational strict slacks and writes \file{CAPPED-OUTER-ARITHMETIC.json}. It rejects five controls: using the complex endpoint without a strict gap, zero group guard, zero boundary slack, retaining the former $Vd$ row, and applying the larger group while still charging the unrecentered $O(ad)$ gauge. The last two distinguish this construction from a numerical reoptimization of the old reduction.

All computational inequalities are strict and hold eventually. Floors, dyadic caps, and integer alpha alter only constants or polylogarithms. For the finite prefix below the common cutoff, the retained elementary multiplication algorithm changes only the constant in the asymptotic statement. This proves Theorem~\ref{thm:main} subject to its stated supplier and interface hypotheses.

\section{Additional corollary from the supplied matrix-exponent theorem}

The first theorem above uses only the fixed seven-product identity for its boundary products. The following further improvement assumes the supplied \emph{Matrix Multiplication in Nine Fourths} theorem, $\omega_{\mathbb C}\leq9/4$, in addition to all of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}'s inherited inputs. Its complete-source and effective-transfer audits are \file{PROOF-AND-COVERAGE.md} and \file{ALGEBRAIC-STABILITY-INDEPENDENT.md}. This is an additional premise, not a consequence of the original finite bit and complex suppliers.

\begin{lemma}[Effective approximate matrix substitution]
Under $\omega_{\mathbb C}\leq9/4$, fix $\tau=19/8$. There is a uniform fixed-description algorithm that multiplies two $W$-square complex dyadic matrices with input magnitude at most $2^h$ to absolute entrywise error $2^{-P}$ in
\[
 O\bigl(W^\tau M(P+h+\log(W+1))\bigr)
\]
bit operations, using $O(P+h+\log W)$ working bits per scalar. Here $M$ is the retained regular unconditional short-integer multiplication bound.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Strict exponent slack supplies fixed integers $m,r$ with an exact rank-$r$ formula and $r<m^\tau$. Its rank equations have integer coefficients. The weak Nullstellensatz replaces a complex solution by one over the algebraic closure of the rationals. A dovetailed enumeration of algebraic tuples and exact tests of these finitely many equations therefore terminates, giving one computable fixed block formula. This search cost is independent of the growing input. Each fixed algebraic coefficient has a fixed isolated simple-root description and is approximated once by precision-doubling Newton iteration in $O(M(P'))$ time at precision $P'$.

Recursion gives $T(W)\leq rT(W/m)+O(W^2)$, with any logarithmic equality case absorbed by the strict exponent slack. The rounding envelope satisfies $E_j\leq K E_{j-1}+K m^{j-1}$ for a formula-dependent fixed $K$, hence $E_j=W^{O(1)}$. Fractional precision $P+2h+O(\log W)$ gives absolute error $2^{-P}$, and intermediate magnitudes are $W^{O(1)}\max(1,2^{2h})$. Only the current square product is padded to the next fixed-base power, at constant volume ratio. Fixed-tape block scans and depth-first scheduling fit the same recurrence, or their logarithms are absorbed by selecting the formula strictly below $\tau$. No tensor axis is padded by this construction.
\end{proof}

In the boundary calculation, $P,h=O(p)$. Since $V$ is \emph{bit volume}, the resulting normalized cost is
\[
 O\bigl(V(d/B)W^{\tau-1}[M(p)/p]\plog p\bigr)
 =O\bigl(Vp^{\epsilon-\xi+11/16}\plog p\bigr).
\]
The factor $M(p)/p$, not $M(p)$, is the per-bit charge. The old residual proof applies to the absolute matrix-product error after a fixed guard enlargement. No Gaussian operator or support set changes.

Retain $q,r_0,\zeta$ and put $s_U=10^{-5}$. For this corollary alone choose
\begin{align*}
 \xi_M&=\frac{3/2+q-(1+q)(r_0+\zeta)+s_U}{2+q},\\
 \epsilon_M&=\frac{1+q(1-\xi_M-r_0-\zeta)}{1+q},\\
 \beta_M&=1-\xi_M-r_0-\zeta.
\end{align*}
Numerically these are
\[
 \epsilon_M=0.998745145709950482,\quad
 \xi_M=0.750213747912678130,\quad
 \beta_M=0.249785242087321870.
\]

\begin{corollary}[Additional matrix-conditioned saving]\label{cor:matrix}
Under Theorem~\ref{thm:main}'s hypotheses and the supplied additional bound $\omega_{\mathbb C}\leq9/4$, the same construction with the preceding parameters runs in
\[
 O\bigl(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa_M}\bigr),\qquad
 \boxed{\kappa_M=0.001673360105405778.}
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
All previously proved parameterized geometry and precision lemmas apply. The individual $K$-neighborhoods still fit their original axes, and total support $O(g\plog p)$ is $o(p)$. The cap satisfies $1/2<\xi_M<\epsilon_M$ and $\beta_M+\xi_M+r_0=1-\zeta$. Membership work has exponent
\[
 \beta_M+2(1-\epsilon_M)<0.253<1,
\]
so it is absorbed by one $p$-bit record. The union fraction tends to zero since $\xi_M-\beta_M-1/2>0.000428$. The old core-face cost has exponent $\epsilon_M+\beta_M-3<-1.75$.

The main and grouped Gaussian savings are equal, while the sparse-union saving has an exact $s_U$ surplus:
\begin{align*}
 \epsilon_Mq&=1-\epsilon_M+q\beta_M,\\
 1-\epsilon_M-\beta_M-1/2+\xi_M&=\epsilon_Mq+s_U.
\end{align*}
Their minimum equals
\[
 0.001673360115405778453817047951720376\ldots>\kappa_M+10^{-11}.
\]
The new boundary saving is $5/16+\xi_M-\epsilon_M>0.0639$, so it is not binding. Global routing, group scans, packed products and core-face repairs have strictly larger savings.

The optional full-key surcharge in the earlier conservative table is absent here: the actual sparse-union algorithm extracts complete rectangles $U_i$, transposes one field, and performs an ordered merge. It does not sort union records. In contrast, all sparse \emph{microhalo} radix keys remain paid in their negligible correction volume. Adding a full-key sort on the union is an explicit rejecting control; omitting it follows from the layout proof, not from the matrix exponent. The new parameter range and q-image ordering are independently checked in \file{MATRIX-LAYOUT-SIGNOFF.md}.

The exact ledger \file{check_matrix_corollary.py} verifies 47 positive strict slacks and six rejecting controls, recorded in \file{MATRIX-COROLLARY-ARITHMETIC.json}. The gain over the upstream selected saving is $6.9990832886\times10^{-7}$. The gain over the separate Strassen result is $4.37755816907\times10^{-7}$. The strict minimum gap absorbs all remaining fixed logarithms as before.
\end{proof}

Corollary~\ref{cor:matrix} retains its explicit additional matrix-exponent premise. The first theorem and its separate reviewed arithmetic receipt remain unchanged.
